question.text: Which of the following fee-structure concepts is NOT a primary testable concept at the Cat I/II AIF manager level (XIX-D scope)?

answer.text: High-Water Mark crystallisation on daily-NAV basis

explanation.text: The Logic: Hurdle rate, clawback, catch-up clauses and deal-by-deal or end-of-tenure waterfalls are all source-backed mechanics for Cat I/II AIFs. High-Water Mark itself is also source-backed for Cat I/II Managers — it is generally applied at portfolio-company exit in deal-by-deal waterfalls. What is NOT a Cat I/II mechanic is daily-NAV CRYSTALLISATION of the HWM, which is the Cat III hedge-fund-style approach. The Trap: The non-keyed options are all standard Cat I/II fee-structure concepts. The keyed option targets the specific daily-NAV crystallisation mechanic that does not fit closed-ended Cat I/II illiquid waterfalls. Note: HWM as a Cat I/II safeguard (at exit, in deal-by-deal waterfalls) is in scope; only the daily-NAV crystallisation form is outside the Cat I/II framework.
